key_insight: OpenForgeRL makes it possible to train AI agents end-to-end using the same complex, stateful harnesses they use at inference time. In short, it bridges the gap between powerful agent runtimes and open-source RL/SFT training stacks.
problem_solved: Most open training infrastructure cannot natively represent multi-turn, multi-process, tool-using harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, or OpenClaw. This makes it difficult to train harness-based agents directly in realistic environments.
method: Provides an open-source framework for end-to-end training of harness-based agents.
Supports stateful, multi-process harness inference within open SFT/RL workflows.
Enables agents to learn in diverse environments while preserving the inference behavior used in deployment.
impact: This matters because practitioners can now train agents in a way that better matches real deployment behavior, reducing the mismatch between training and inference. It lowers the barrier to building more capable, tool-using agents with open infrastructure.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram of standard RL training vs. harness-native training

Icon set for agent, harness, tools, and environment connections
Before/after illustration of training-inference mismatch being removed
paper_title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
paper_authors: Xiao Yu, Baolin Peng, Ruize Xu, Hao Zou, Qianhui Wu
